claims.statement: For the exact registered lower-region target and fixed selector, the route's aggregate admits the identity S(T,p)=sum_{|B|=p+1} w_F(B)-sum_{|B|=p} w_F(B); saturation of its described cross-tag deletion graph would suffice for S(T,p)<=0, but no saturation bound or counterexample is established.
claims.scope: Finite ordinary trees T and natural p satisfying x(T)+2<=p and 3p<2alpha(T)+1, with zero-extended independence counts, original supports and neighborhoods, strict selector F(T,p), and distinct original-leaf tags; the identity is exact and the matching assertion is only conditional.
claims.reason: Disposition: retained_narrowed. Independent derivation confirms the q-rank and fixed-selector weighted-rank identities, including same-support multiplicities, and the matching-saturation implication. The route omits the required Hall/capacity proof and gives no eligible positive complete sum, so it does not resolve the registered universal inequality.

limitations: No cross-tag Hall inequality, matching, or fractional capacity estimate is proved under the fixed favorable selector.
No eligible positive full-sum counterexample is supplied; failure of the proposed matching alone would not refute the primary assertion.
The critique establishes no universal verdict and uses no external theorem or computation.
